text:
sam: Drafting a deterministic decision graph for tenant routing across regions. Need to factor: residency_tag, consent_flag, dataset_cache_policy, write_policy, cost_budget, and operator overrides. Sharing a compact sketch. Feedback? :thinking:

sam: ```
start -> residency_check
  -> if residency==EU -> enforce eu_write_path
  -> else -> consent_check
    -> if consent==no_transfer -> local_only_reads_and_writes
    -> else -> cost_budget_check
      -> if budget_ok -> latency_cost_tradeoff
        -> prefer nearest_region unless write_policy==STRICT_RESIDENCY
      -> else -> best_effort_hosted + operator_alert
```

mara: Nice. A few clarifications: 1) "local_only_reads_and_writes" still needs a read-optimisation path for low-latency reads inside region (edge cache). 2) For datasets flagged as PII, reads must not be cached cross-region. Suggest a dataset tag `cacheable_by_policy` and `pii_level` (high/low).

lee: Agree on tags. Also: operator overrides must be auditable and have policy constraints. Suggest we represent overrides as a structured audit event: override_id, actor, reason_code, expires_at, scope. Must be emitted to the audit log and trigger a telemetry metric `override_applied`.

olivia: Add cost budget earlier in the graph so we avoid routing that would exceed monthly commit. If cost_budget is close to limit, route to lighter-weight quantized model variant or restrict to hosted. Also: add header versioning e.g. `X-Routing-Graph: v2026-03-23-01` so we can replay decisions later for forensics.

sam: Good point. Update order: residency -> consent -> cost_budget_check -> dataset_cache_policy -> latency_cost_tradeoff -> final_route. We'll include `X-Routing-Graph` and `final_routing_reason` in response headers.

mara: Edge-case: active-active write acceptance. For tenants with residency==EU, we should not accept writes in non-EU primaries unless tenant has token-level consent and `write_policy==ALLOW_ESCROW_WRITE`. Otherwise writes must be proxied to EU primary.

lee: Implement a KMS-region validation on cross-region writes: if encryption_key.region != target_region then deny unless `escrow_flag` set and operator_approved. That protects SLA and compliance.

sam: Operator override matrix idea: OVR-EMERGENCY-24H (scope:tenant, requires_2fa:true, expires:24h, reason:[emergency_failover,cost_spike]). Devops-bot: add telemetry hooks for `decision_node` and `override_audit` events.

olivia: Also recommend a sticky decision window (5 minutes) to avoid oscillation when latency/cost signals flip during transient spikes. Record `decision_version` and `sticky_until` for each tenant route record.

lee: I'll sketch a tiny simulation harness: generate 10k synthetic tenants with mixed residency/consent/dataset policies, inject a region outage, run the routing graph, and measure percent of tenants that violated residency or hit operator overrides. That should guide thresholds for `latency_cost_tradeoff` and sticky window length.

mara: For marking datasets, propose adding two flags in dataset metadata: `cacheable_by_policy: [true|false]` and `pii_class: [none,low,high]`. Our proxy should only serve cacheable items cross-region and only if pii_class != high.

sam: Action items: 1) I will update the graph with cost_budget and dataset checks and publish v2026-03-23-01. 2) @lee draft override audit event spec and simulation harness outline. 3) @mara propose dataset metadata fields and validation in catalog. 4) @olivia add header stubbing in proxy and ensure telemetry keys. 5) Devops-bot to make sure audit events are emitted on manual overrides.

devops-bot: checklist: emit `routing_graph_version`, `decision_node`, `final_routing_reason`, `override_audit` events. Ensure audit writes are replicated to long-term storage.

sam: I'll open an RFC follow-up with the updated ASCII graph, the simulation plan, and a short operator-runbook for override handling. Thanks all :thumbsup:
